column1: # Wake-ups per second each thread of an idle Dusk Studio may cost, checked by
# thread-name<TAB>ceiling record per line; threads of one name count together,
# and a trailing number in a name is an index, written as *. A ceiling is
# wake-ups per second, or <n>/block for a thread the audio clock drives: n
# wake-ups per audio block at the rate and quantum the device opened with.
# Re-record after a fix with: bash scripts/regress/idle-wakeups.sh --update
# It only lowers ceilings and drops names that no longer run. Raising a ceiling
# or adding a name is a hand edit, and the change has to say why.
# Recorded on an 8-core box (six DSP pool workers), 48000 Hz at quantum 512, on
# Xvfb, where Mesa's llvmpipe threads draw the window.
# DuskStudio is the framework's timer thread, which wakes twice for each
# deadline. Every dusk::Timer shares one 30 Hz tick now; most of what is left is
# the framework's own timers: the X11 window's vblank timer, which runs at its
# 100 Hz fallback because Xvfb reports a 0 Hz mode, and the tooltip window's.
